extracted.intended_audience: merit review committee members, research funders, research administrators, and researchers applying for SSHRC/Tri-agency funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing scholarly research (especially SSHRC-funded social sciences, humanities, and interdisciplinary projects) in ways that de-emphasize journal metrics and recognize diverse outputs, impacts, and responsible research practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of scientific content over journal metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific content of a paper is always more important than publication metrics or the identity of the journal in which it was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unintended overuse of journal publication as a primary indicator of quality. Committee members should judge quality on the substantive content rather than journal impact factors or prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize a variety of research outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality research outcomes are achieved in many ways, including, but not limited to: publishing research articles; reporting new knowledge (such as presenting at conferences and other venues); sharing data; contributing to policy decisions and improvements in practice; producing highly trained personnel; working in partnership with various sectors of society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merit review should consider the value and impact of all research outputs in addition to traditional publications. Assessors should explicitly account for outputs such as datasets, presentations, training outcomes, and community partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess influence on policy and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Research assessment should consider influence on policy and practice as a valid form of impact and evidence of research value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include documented contributions to policy decisions, practice improvements, and other real-world impacts when evaluating proposals and past performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value research training and capacity building
rubrics_metrics.description: Producing highly trained personnel and effective research training are important research outcomes that should factor into assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate contributions to trainee development, mentorship, and the broader capacity-building role of a project; consider SSHRC's Guidelines for effective research training as relevant guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for partnerships and multisectoral engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Working in partnership with various sectors of society (e.g., industry, government, community organizations) is a valuable research outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the quality and relevance of partnerships and their contribution to research impact, knowledge mobilization, and translation into practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include non-refereed, forthcoming, creative outputs and professional contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are encouraged to consider a variety of research contributions, including traditional academic publications, non-refereed and forthcoming contributions, creative outputs and other relevant services and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss non-traditional or in-progress outputs; give appropriate weight to forthcoming work, creative outputs, and service/experience that demonstrate contribution and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use discipline-sensitive assessment tools and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment tools and guidelines should reflect the understanding that the nature of valuable research outcomes varies between disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ assessment guides tailored to discipline-specific norms and outcomes; avoid one-size-fits-all criteria that privilege certain output types over others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multidisciplinary and multisectoral review committees for interdisciplinary work
rubrics_metrics.description: TIPS programs rely on multidisciplinary and multisectoral committees for merit review; assessment guides help evaluate proposals in various disciplines and those with an interdisciplinary approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For interdisciplinary or multisectoral proposals, convene review panels with appropriate breadth of expertise and use guidance that recognizes interdisciplinary methods, outputs, and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate responsible research practices into assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC aligns with DORA through initiatives on research data management; open access; responsible conduct of research; ethical conduct of research involving humans; and equity, diversity, inclusion and accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should recognize and reward good practices such as open access, robust data management, ethical conduct, and attention to equity, diversity, inclusion and accessibility as part of research quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize Indigenous research practices and context-sensitive guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC’s Guidelines for the merit review of Indigenous research acknowledge the importance of a variety of types of research outputs and culturally appropriate evaluation approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating Indigenous research, apply guidelines that respect Indigenous ways of knowing and evaluate outputs and impacts in culturally appropriate terms rather than only conventional academic metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support research-creation and knowledge mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC has a history of support for research-creation across funding opportunities and promotion of knowledge mobilization in various forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give explicit consideration to creative research outputs and active knowledge mobilization strategies (e.g., engagement, dissemination beyond academia) when assessing proposals and accomplishments.
